# windowsddi_dns_ptr_record (Resource)

Manages the PTR (reverse lookup) record of one name in a zone, for example name `80` in zone `20.1.10.in-addr.arpa` for 10.1.20.80. Extra PTR records of the name are removed.

The resource is authoritative for every PTR record of its name: records of that name and type that are not in the configuration are removed. Creating it fails when such records already exist, so existing records are adopted with `terraform import` instead; dynamic records (registered by clients or the DHCP server) can be replaced with `allow_overwrite_dynamic`.

Updates are not atomic: new values are added first, then TTLs are updated, then old values are removed, so the name never resolves empty. A failure midway leaves a mix of old and new values, which the next plan shows and corrects.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# PTR for 10.1.20.80 in the 20.1.10.in-addr.arpa zone.
resource "windowsddi_dns_ptr_record" "www" {
  zone_name = "20.1.10.in-addr.arpa"
  name      = "80"
  target    = "www.lab.example.local"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Record name relative to the zone, for example `www`, or `@` for the zone apex. Case is ignored. Changing it replaces the resource.
- `target` (String) Host name the address resolves to, for example `www.lab.example.local`. Fully qualified; a trailing dot is optional and case is ignored.
- `zone_name` (String) Zone holding the records, for example `lab.example.local`. Case and a trailing dot are ignored. Changing it replaces the resource.

### Optional

- `allow_overwrite_dynamic` (Boolean) When `true`, creating the resource replaces existing dynamic records of the name (registered by clients or the DHCP server) instead of failing. Static records are never overwritten. Defaults to `false`. Terraform only, not read from the server.
- `ttl` (Number) Time to live in seconds, applied to every record of the set (1 to 2147483647). When unset, the zone default is used on create and the server's value is reported.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) `<zone_name>/<name>` in lowercase, the import ID.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import ID: <zone>/<name>, with @ for the zone apex.
terraform import windowsddi_dns_ptr_record.80 20.1.10.in-addr.arpa/80
```
